spans.text: Foom!
The window reflects a roaring blaze, replacing the blackness of night with the scorching red sky.
Pfagh... (Coughs heavily)
Wait, get...Get off me!
Are you out of your mind?!
A human would die in this fire!
ST AR-15 drags J out of the building by force. The Commander rushes over to him.
J!
Let me go... Let me go!
Please, I'm begging you... Nele...Nele is still in there!
Calm down!
The signal interference has been neutralized and I've informed the fire department and the police.
They ought to be here soon.
(Pants and coughs)
Having inhaled smoke, J shrugs off ST AR-15's hands and keeps muttering to himself in a daze as he looks up at the apartment, which is burning merrily.
It isn't just him. The fire is too much even for the Dolls.
Another piece of glass is shattered. A dark figure bursts out of the apartment window, landing firmly on the ground.
M16 dusts off the small sparks on her and shrugs.
...Might as well give up. I'm pretty damn certain there are no survivors in there.
J stares blankly at Nele's floor, where the fire started.
...It's all my fault.
The Commander does not console him.
It is precisely because they feel the same way that they know that there is no consoling him.
"I'm going to take responsibility for this Idunn thing."
Why should she take responsibility...?
She's not an agent or a soldier, she wasn't even involved in this whole business.
All of us are prepared to die, but she wasn't. She was just an ordinary person that I dragged into this mess!
She was so young, and she wouldn't have done something this dangerous if not for me...
I used her... I used her idealism...
She was just a civilian...
God, I've had it... What the hell am I even doing...?
In the furthest reaches of pain, J suddenly bursts into creepy laughter.
On either side of J, the much-delayed firefighters rush to put out the blaze.
His surroundings grow noisier and noisier, but his mind drifts further and further away.
First it was his subordinates, then Mona, and now Nele.
He's always making someone else pay the price in his place...
Making them pay the price for his recklessness and presumption...
...There is no hope in J's eyes.
J puts a hand on a nearby lamp post as he feels a sudden, intense surge rising from his gut, into his throat—
(Heaves)
All the suppressed trauma he's accumulated up till now comes gushing out in this moment of mental breakdown.
Hey.
...Leave me alone.
A hand rests on his shoulder...
Someone is patting him.
...I said, leave me alone.
Give me some peace and quiet...
What do you mean?
Why are you throwing up on my doorstep...
I told you to leave me alo—?!
Unable to bear it anymore, J jerks his head back in anger, and just as he's about to launch into a tirade—
J's eyes go wide in utter disbelief.
...Nele?
Commander, I think I'm hallucinating.
...Are you stupid or something?
I liked you better when you were a jerk...
What...The hell is going on?
Didn't you want to know who I was?
...I think I have a rough idea.
To think you would be sharper than everyone else here.
I knew it... You're not Mrs. Gray after all.
Nele smiles in relief and meets Gray's gaze fearlessly. In fact, she's almost emboldened by it.
Thank goodness.
All this time, I didn't know how I'd confront you about this, but now, I'm relieved.
That's the "Technical Theory of Biological Human Automation", isn't it?
You really are a bright one.
I'm proud of my eye for talent.
I see. That field of research is practically forbidden.
Your very existence is an ethical violation.
Nele takes a step back and quickly unplugs the hard disk she connected to the PC.
Database 100% complete.
Do you think you can walk out of here with that?
If you kill me now, what will Eicher think? He's right outside. He saw me meet you here with his own eyes.
That will be my problem.
Gray calmly sizes up the girl in front of her.
If I'd known you cared so much about this woman, I would have reunited the two of you long ago.
Since you've earned my recognition, you have three sentences before you die.
That's nowhere near enough—
Hard disk in hand, Nele takes a few steps back until she nears the window, where she suddenly lets go of it. The hard disk slides down a pipe into a densely-packed region of vegetation.
Looks like the police will be coming by to issue us a ticket for high-rise littering.
But don't worry, I will be very happy to retrieve that item.
You have two sentences left.
If I were you, I'd retrieve that hard disk now.
There's no rush.
In just a few minutes, the main entrance will be surrounded by reporters, here to interview Mrs. Gray, the chairwoman of Galatea Corporation, who's been incommunicado for a long time.
Looks like I have your attention. May I?
Interesting. I'm lifting the limit. Proceed.
I know that amount of time is more than enough for you to silence me, but is it really enough for you to hide my body?
And then there's that evidence which has fallen somewhere on the grounds.
While I don't know why, you've been trying to stay off the news recently, am I right?
...You've got guts.
I simply want to live.
I want to live, so that I can make sense of all this.
Nele gulps.
I was right about you, Nele.
You aren't just intelligent, but talented too.
Gray smiles at Nele, and an almost imperceptible sound comes from behind her.
In a Stasi interrogation room.
...What happened next? Well, a horde of reporters poured into the building.
I met Mia when I was going downstairs and she kept me safe until we got outside. I wouldn't have made it otherwise.
I knew that woman wouldn't let me go—I wasn't stupid enough to go home.
Smart. Almost too smart.
K puts away his notepad and gives Nele a thumbs up.
You're certainly much smarter than someone I know.
Who do you mean?
Oh, it's nothing. We understand the situation now.
Thank you for your contribution to the security of the State. The Stasi will be taking charge of your personal safety from now on.
We will not let your life come under any danger.
I'll be counting on you, then... Frankly speaking, my legs are still trembling, even now.
Still, it's not too bad. I'll have to find a new apartment, but I didn't lose too much.
After he finishes taking her statement, K soothes Nele again and leaves the interrogation room with his notepad.
Outside the interrogation room, J is pacing back and forth restlessly. The moment he sees K, he immediately rushes up to him.
I truly did not expect to be called back because of something like this.
K slaps the notepad into J's chest, his face filled with exasperation.
...I'm sorry, I screwed up really badly.
In a rare turn of events, J makes no rebuke. Instead, he takes the document without a word.
K takes in J's pensiveness and pats him on the shoulder.
Don't take it too hard.
At least the girl's still alive, isn't she?
Yeah.
J takes a deep breath.
...And thank God for that.
